findings.finding: when the un-stamped card is merged into `unresolvedTest` and spliced out of `cards`/`testCards`, the spliced card itself is not removed from `state.failedTestCards` (or from `authoringConsumedBy` values / `restoreValidationPending`). The in-file trace argues no card can re-enter this function, and the sets die with the derivation, so this is inert today — but it is the exact "detached card referenced by resolver state" hazard the 40th/43rd rounds were policing, left half-guarded on the merged-away side.
findings.suggestion: add `state.failedTestCards.delete(card)` next to the two `splice` calls (defence-in-depth, two lines, no reachable behavior change), or extend the existing comment to say the merged-away card is deliberately left in the set.

findings.file: client/src/components/external/mission/MissionActivityFeed.test.tsx` — "remounts a card that changes kind" test
findings.finding: the test's guarantee depends entirely on the entry `key` in `MissionActivityFeed.tsx` leading with `card.kind`, which is outside this diff. The test does falsify a regression, so this is sound, but the contract lives cross-file with no in-source marker at the key itself (the comment lives only in the test and in `FeedCard`'s state comment).
findings.suggestion: a one-line comment at the `key={...}` site in `MissionActivityFeed.tsx` noting that kind-first ordering is load-bearing for `detailExpanded` reset would make the coupling visible where a future edit would happen.  Spec compliance: all five requirements are implemented and test-pinned — (1) the completed-run `OperationCard`/`mission-completed-stack` mount is removed unconditionally with the designgate surface untouched; (2) `FeedCommands` collapses behind an "N commands" toggle for every count including 1; (3) `card.text`/`card.explanation` route through `MarkdownChunk` with the `textLiteral` exception exactly as scoped; (4) the blocker derives a plain-language headline via `summarizeBlockerError` with the raw output/command behind a collapsed disclosure; (5) authoring runs are excluded from the gate stamp at both the resolve and reconcile levels, including the failing-red-step and failed-write-rollback cases. Security posture is preserved: synthesized text renders as React text children, raw output in `<pre>`, markdown only through the sanitized pipeline, with inertness tests carried over.  SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: approve

findings.finding: A “freshly-written test file” remains eligible for six subsequent tool calls, so a later targeted verification run can be marked `authoringRun` and lose its Passing/Failing treatment despite not being the first run immediately after authoring. For example: write `foo.test.ts`, perform several unrelated edits/reads, then run `vitest foo.test.ts`.
findings.suggestion: Restrict the exemption to the immediate TDD sequence more tightly (for example, consume/clear it on unrelated mutating work), or otherwise require direct adjacency as specified.

findings.finding: sameTestFilePath` suffix-matches any absolute write path to a bare relative test target. In a monorepo, writing `/repo/packages/api/src/foo.test.ts` and then running root-level `src/foo.test.ts` incorrectly matches, suppressing the real verification card’s gate status.
findings.suggestion: Thread the shell working directory/project root into path resolution, then compare canonical paths. Until that is available, avoid treating ambiguous bare relative suffixes as the same file.  Overall assessment: ship-with-fixes. The UI requirements are otherwise implemented, but the authoring-run exemption can suppress legitimate verification status in concrete workflows.  SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: revise
